Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Myers: Hey everyone thanks for joining, let's do quick intros and then jump into the cost model, Samira and I will lead.
[00:12] Alicia Gomez: Hi, Alicia here. We're excited to scope the POC, thanks Jordan.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Marcus here, CTO. I'll be watching the throughput/infra bits.
[00:22] Priya Reddy: Priya, SRE. I'll need the network and VPC details, k m s for keys.
[00:30] Samira Patel: Hi, Samira, SE on Redwood. Today we'll walk through expected traffic, then model per-token economics, then benchmarks and timelines.
[00:38] Jordan Myers: Quick agenda: 1) baseline workload sizing 2) cost assumptions 3) knobs to tune (batching, caching, quant) 4) bench plan and success criteria 5) next steps.
[01:02] Alicia Gomez: For context our main use-case is an interactive assistant inside our B2B product. Typical user session is 4-6 turns, average input length ~40 tokens, model response ~220 tokens, 80% of calls single-turn. Peak--we can hit 120 rps for a short period but avg sustained ~15 rps.
[01:28] Samira Patel: Good, that's helpful. When you say 220 tokens response, is that before any summarization? and do you have prompt templates?
[01:36] Alicia Gomez: Yes that's full response, we do add system prompt about 50 tokens and some few-shot examples ~120 tokens in about 30% of calls, so sequence length varies.
[01:46] Jordan Myers: Ok so seq len distribution: median ~200, 90th ~480, tail occasionally near 1k. That will affect KV cache hit rates and batching efficiency.
[01:58] Marcus Lee: Important for us: budget is $10k/month for the pilot, and we need to understand per-token unit economics so we can forecast scale.
[02:08] Jordan Myers: Understood. We'll walk through two pricing scenarios: hosted API (pay-as-you-go) and dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs). Hosted has higher per-token marginal but no infra ops; dedicated lowers per-token cost but has commit and utilization considerations.
[02:24] Samira Patel: First, baseline per-token estimates. For a vanilla open model running on our hosted infra, rough starting number is $0.0006 per input token and $0.0012 per output token for a 13B-like model V2. That's before batching/caching. With 220 output tokens on average that's ~0.26 cents per request in outputs plus inputs.
[02:46] Priya Reddy: Those numbers seem high compared to some public benchmarks. Are you assuming quantized execution or FP16?
[02:52] Samira Patel: Good question. The hosted baseline assumes FP16 on A100/p optimized kernels. If you enable 8-bit or 4-bit quantization we can push costs down 20-40% depending on model fidelity needs.
[03:06] Alicia Gomez: How much does batching help? Our calls are mostly interactive so we worry about latency.
[03:13] Jordan Myers: Right, for interactive with strict P95 latency SLOs, batching is minimal. Our continuous-batching helps combine nearby requests with sub-25ms queuing sometimes, but aggressive batching adds tail latency. For your mix, we estimate effective batching gain ~5-10% on tokens. If you accept slightly higher P95 we can tune to reach 20-30% token reduction.
[03:36] Marcus Lee: What about KV cache / prefix caching for repeated context? We have many similar prompts in a session.
[03:42] Samira Patel: KV cache can be a big win. If you have repeated system prompt + few-shot context, the runtime can reuse KV cache, which reduces compute per token for repeated prefixes. In practice we often see 15-35% token cost reduction for session-based assistants. Note some customers misreport this; also transcriber note: sometimes k v cache gets written as k v cash in docs.
[04:02] Priya Reddy: For the dedicated option, what's the reserve profile and how to think about utilization?
[04:08] Jordan Myers: Typical dedicated offer is a pool of GPUs with a monthly commit. If you commit to 8x A100-equivalent, your per-token can drop by ~40-60% compared to hosted, but you'll need ~60-70% utilization to justify. We can model breakeven points in the spreadsheet I'll send.
[04:26] Alicia Gomez: Can you show a sample cost calc for our numbers? Using 15 rps sustained, avg 260 tokens total per request (inputs+outputs), 30 days.
[04:36] Samira Patel: Sure quick back-of-envelope: 15 rps * 3600 * 24 * 30 = ~39M requests/month. Wait that seems off, sorry, that's for 15 rps sustained 24/7. If your user traffic is 12 hours active window, it's about half. Let's assume active 12h/day: ~19.5M requests/month. At ~260 tokens/request => ~5.07B tokens/month. At hosted blended $0.001 per token (weighted inputs/outputs) that's ~$5k/mo. That fits your $10k/month pilot cap with room for QC and experimentation. (transcription note: speaker overlap -> "we're at five k" was used).
[05:10] Marcus Lee: Hmm that's better than expected. But peak spikes may push latency. What SLAs for P95?
[05:17] Jordan Myers: Our SLA for hosted P95 is region-dependent; for the POC we'll target P95 < 350ms on typical prompts. We'll include fallback to smaller models for spikes; we also recommend prefix caching and light batching.
[05:30] Alicia Gomez: About benchmarks  what do you need from us and what's the plan?
[05:34] Samira Patel: We need: sample prompts, sample traffic distribution (seq len histogram and requests per minute over a week), and a success criteria doc with metrics (P95 latency target, quality thresholds like BLEU or manual eval pass rates). Our plan: 1) run a 1-hour baseline on Redwood sandbox (hosted) with your samples, collect latency/throughput/cost per token 2) run a 4-hour stress run including spike windows 3) optionally run quantized model and dedicated capacity estimate. We'll share results and a modeled forecast.
[06:02] Priya Reddy: For security we need SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML options, KMS integration, and support for private VPC connectors.
[06:10] Jordan Myers: We'll attach our security pack. For POCs we can enable a private sandbox with VPC peering and KMS integration; full on-prem package takes longer. We'll share SOC2 and the architecture notes.
[06:22] Marcus Lee: Are there any gotchas on data residency? We're EU customers so we'll need Europe region availability.
[06:28] Samira Patel: We're available in EU regions; we can pin routing to EU-only and ensure logs are kept in region for the pilot. We'll include audit log retention options too.
[06:40] Alicia Gomez: On quality regression  do you run evals to compare model variants? We want to ensure quant doesn't degrade user experience.
[06:46] Samira Patel: Yes we can run side-by-side evals on your test set. Our Optimize tooling provides regression alerts vs a baseline prompt set; we'll tie quality thresholds to rollout policies, can recommend model + quantization profiles where quality delta < 2%.
[07:02] Jordan Myers: Let's talk concrete knobs and expected savings: quantization 4-bit -> 25-40% cost saving, batching up to 30% but with latency tradeoff, KV cache 15-35% for session-heavy workloads, model distillation or smaller family could reduce cost further at possible quality tradeoff.
[07:24] Priya Reddy: For the benchmark, how will costs be measured? Token-level, GPU-hours, or both?
[07:29] Samira Patel: We'll report both: tokens consumed, wall-clock GPU time, and expressed as $/1M tokens. Also show latency percentiles and per-request cost.
[07:38] Alicia Gomez: Timeline: we want to start next week and have results two weeks after start. Is that feasible?
[07:44] Jordan Myers: For a tight timeline: share traffic and prompts by Wed (2026-12-08), we'll run an initial 1-hour benchmark by 2026-12-10, deliver results and cost model by 2026-12-14, then a follow-up on 2026-12-17 to decide pilot configuration. That fits a 2-week cadence.
[07:58] Marcus Lee: Regarding procurement: if we go dedicated, what's the minimum commitment length?
[08:03] Jordan Myers: Typically 3 or 12 month reserved commitment. For pilots we do a 1-2 month evaluation with month-to-month reserved capacity to get utilization data, then recommend longer commit if beneficial.
[08:14] Alicia Gomez: Any examples of similar customers?
[08:17] Jordan Myers: We recently did a POC with "Horizon Analytics" where caching and quantization got them to 45% unit cost reduction  I can share anonymized numbers.
[08:27] Priya Reddy: Ok next steps recap?
[08:30] Jordan Myers: Jordan will send cost model spreadsheet and sample prompt template by 2026-12-07. Samira will stand up a Redwood sandbox and run a 1-hour benchmark by 2026-12-10. Alicia will share traffic patterns and success criteria by 2026-12-08. We'll schedule a results review the following week.
[08:46] Alicia Gomez: Sounds good. One more question: do you have built-in retry/failover to smaller models during spikes?
[08:52] Samira Patel: Yes, smart routing supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants or to regional pools, with configurable policies. We'll demo that in the follow-up.
[09:02] Marcus Lee: Great. Appreciate you mapping to our budget.
[09:06] Jordan Myers: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the spreadsheet and security pack.
[09:12] (call ends)
